title: Potato leaf miner on Irish potato

Header: Potato leaf miner on Irish potato
Liriomyza spp. (Potato leaf miner) Urunyo rw'ibirayi

Prevention: Plough and hoe the soil at least one week before planting so that any of the insects resting will be dried by the sun and will die.
Leaf miners are highly polyphagous and feed on many plant species
Excessive application renders plant more susceptible to damage by this pest.
Destroy alternate hosts, including weeds, and infected plant material e.g. mined leaves
Crop rotation with carrot as leaf miners don't like them
Tunnel damage on potato leaves. (Photo by
Monitoring: Perform regular scouting of field to monitor the presence of flies and/or young miners on leaves by looking the tunnels that are grey-brown in colour.
Check the young stage of insects living and feeding inside the leaves
Use yellow sticky traps to monitor adult population
Direct Control: Put yellow sticky traps to catch the adult insect:
Weather proof or cardboard sheet and paint it yellow cover with castor oil or petroleum jelly.; Suspend it above the crop; Put them every 2 to 3 meters distance; Change the traps every week
Pick and destroy all infested leaves, Use a neem based pesticides such as

Neem seed extract (Azadirachtin): 60 gr per 1liter of water; Spray to just about covering the plant once a week until the problem is gone; Azadirachtin, rate of 25 gr per litre of water, spray it weekly
Restrictions: Use of pesticides to control vectors (whiteflies) on cassava is not pratical: insecticides can kill natural enemies such as
Apoanagyrus lopezi (released before 1990 to control cassava mealybugs) and
Typhlodromalus aripo (natural enemy of cassava green mites).
Protection equipments (PPE) and follow the instructions on the product label.
